audit.whatIsWrong: Twisted Advance makes Maokai untargetable while he dashes, and that word appears nowhere on the page — it is described only as a root. Sap Magic, the passive that actually heals him on attack and whose cooldown shortens every time he casts a spell or is hit by one, is never named; the page credits his sustain to 'saplings' three times, and saplings do not heal. Ionian Fervor is called an on-hit armour shred in five places; Riot's text is stacking attack speed plus bonus on-hit damage, with no resistance reduction anywhere in Irelia's kit. None of his five abilities are named in the content layer at all.
audit.why: Untargetability is the difference between a spent ultimate and a kill: an Irelia who fires Flawless Duet or Bladesurge into the dash loses the whole commit. And a player who thinks her passive shreds armour will keep auto-attacking a stacked tank expecting his resistances to fall.
audit.corrected: Twisted Advance's untargetable frames written into the win condition, wants.you[0] and mid; Sap Magic named as the real sustain with the Grievous Wounds answer; every Ionian Fervor 'shred' replaced with the attack-speed stacking it actually is; Bramble Smash, Sapling Toss and Nature's Grasp named in the content prose.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three chart rows disagreed with the packet and the prose: Level 2 read Irelia while whys[1] opens 'Even still'; Levels 4-5 read Skill while whys[3] says you bully him through his sustain; 2+ items read Irelia while whys[6] says he out-scales you outright.
audit.why: 49.86% over 369 Emerald+ games is even until he itemises, which is exactly the packet chart's shape. The 2+ items row was the reader-facing contradiction: the chart promised the late game to Irelia while the paragraph beside it said the opposite.
audit.corrected: Rows 1, 3 and 6 flipped in both layers as one atomic group, with Levels 4-5 raised to 7/10 and 2+ items dropped to 3/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Trade after his W is on cooldown' is repeated four times without ever giving the cooldown.
audit.why: Twisted Advance is 12 seconds at rank 3 and Bramble Smash only 6 — so the punish window is real but short, and the reader needs the number to use it.
audit.corrected: Twisted Advance's 12s written into wants.you[0] and mid.

edits.before: Level 1 you're both low-impact — he has saplings and passive sustain to trade-tank, you only have Q and no E yet, so just farm with Q-resets off the wave and stay out of his W root-dash range when there's nothing to gain. Don't burn your Q chasing a kill you can't finish; his W is a targeted root-dash that locks you the moment you overstay, and his Q knockback follows it. The lane is genuinely even here — respect the root, last-hit cleanly, and wait for your level 3 E.
edits.after: Level 1 you're both low-impact — Sap Magic heals him back on every empowered attack, you only have Q and no E, so farm Q-resets off the wave and stay out of Twisted Advance (W) range when there's nothing to gain. Don't burn Q chasing a kill you can't finish: Twisted Advance is targeted, he is untargetable while it travels, and Bramble Smash (Q) knockback follows the root. The lane is genuinely even here — respect it, last-hit cleanly, and wait for your level 3 E.

edits.before: This is your window. At 3 your E stun lets you open a trade, Q in for the reset, and beat him before his sustain matters; by 4-5 maxed Q gives you reset uptime off the wave and your passive's stacking on-hit shred melts his early armor. Bait his W root-dash first — once it's down he has no escape and no peel, so E-stun, Q in, and chain resets so he can't disengage. Just respect that he trades evenly and out-sustains chip with his passive, so pick the window after his W is on cooldown rather than poking him at full HP.
edits.after: This is your window. At 3 your E stun opens the trade, Q in for the reset, and by 4-5 maxed Q gives reset uptime off the wave while Ionian Fervor's attack speed ramps. Bait Twisted Advance first and never spend your combo into it — he is untargetable mid-dash, so everything you throw is wasted. Once it's down, that's 12 seconds at rank 3 with no escape and no peel: E-stun, Q in, chain resets. Buy Grievous Wounds, because Sap Magic refills whatever chip you leave behind.

notes: Twisted Advance turns Maokai untargetable and the page never said so — an Irelia who spends Flawless Duet or Bladesurge into the dash loses the entire commit. His sustain was also attributed to saplings three times when it comes from Sap Magic, which heals on his empowered attack and speeds up every time he casts or is hit by a spell — so anti-heal, not poke-avoidance, is the answer. Ionian Fervor was again described as armour shred; it is stacking attack speed plus on-hit damage, matching the correction established on the Malphite mirror. Three chart rows flipped as a matched group, including 2+ items to Maokai, where the chart directly contradicted its own why.
